behavioral_notes.observation: event.booth carries a 2-value Selection state available/unavailable (default 'available', group_expand=True, tracking=True). is_available is a non-stored compute (state=='available') with a custom _search_is_available that maps the 'in'/'not in' operators back onto state='available'/'unavailable' (returning NotImplemented for other operators). The kanban/pivot/graph and the event-level available counters all hang off this single state field; none of that mapping is visible in metadata.

Assigning a booth to a renter is a state transition, not a separate document: action_confirm(additional_values) merges {'state':'unavailable'} with any extra vals and calls write(). write() snapshots booths still 'available' as to_confirm, and after super().write() if the new state is 'unavailable' it calls _action_post_confirm, which posts the 'event_booth.event_booth_booked_template' mail message onto the parent event_id chatter under the mt_event_booth_booked subtype. So booking a booth confirms it (makes it unavailable) AND logs a booked note on the event. This side-effect chain is invisible to metadata.

The customer side is captured by partner_id (string 'Renter', tracking=True, copy=False). contact_name/contact_email/contact_phone are stored, editable computes (readonly=False, copy=False) that default-fill from partner_id.name/email/phone only when still empty, letting an exhibitor contact differ from the renter partner record. create() runs with mail_create_nosubscribe=True and immediately calls _post_confirmation_message for any booth created already-unavailable. Pure code behavior, not in metadata.

On the event.event inherit, event_booth_ids is a stored compute (precompute=True) depending on event_type_id: when the event type changes it emulates an onchange by Command.unlink-ing only booths still is_available and Command.create-ing one event.booth per event_type_booth_ids template line, copying just the whitelisted fields from event.type.booth._get_event_booth_fields_whitelist() (['name','booth_category_id']). _compute_event_booth_count uses a sudo _read_group over event.booth grouped by state to derive event_booth_count and event_booth_count_available without loading rows. event.type.booth._get_default_booth_category auto-assigns the sole booth category when exactly one exists. This template-instantiation logic is not in metadata.

extract_frontend reports no JS/OWL footprint for event_booth: 0 js files, 0 xml templates, 0 owl_components, 0 registry adds, no asset bundles. The module is backend-only and renders entirely through standard Odoo form/list/kanban/pivot/graph views (4 form, 3 list, 1 kanban, 3 search, 1 pivot, 1 graph); any storefront booth-selection UI lives in the separate website_event_booth / event_booth_sale addons.

extract_frontend reports no outbound integration surface: 0 http call sites, no sdk imports, no api keys, no endpoints. event_booth makes no external calls of its own; any payment/map integration is inherited transitively from the event dependency, not introduced here.

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: event_booth is an event value-network extension (Stabell & Fjeldstad): booths are an exhibitor-facing offering mediated through the event platform, not a transformation chain. The economic logic is capacity/availability mediation - a fixed set of booths per event, each toggling available->unavailable as exhibitors are matched to stands, with availability rollups (event_booth_count_available, event_booth_category_available_ids) and chatter promotion of bookings. There is no sequential make-to-deliver production (chain) and no per-case diagnostic work (shop); the module connects exhibitors to event capacity, which is mediating-technology / network logic, inherited from and reinforcing the parent event network. It is a primary, customer-facing activity. APQC 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services is the closest PCF home because selling/allocating exhibitor booth space is a sell motion (event sponsorship/booth sales); the actual paid checkout lives in the separate event_booth_sale / website_event_booth addons, so this base module covers the catalog + assignment portion of that sell process.
